reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) / internal conflict with §8 and the shipped showcase
gaps.problem: Item 12 sets a hard threshold on 'the two crossing 16 m streets at (40, 40)' — paved square <= 34 x 34 m. But (40,40) is not a street/street crossing. §8 item 1 stages the east-west avenue through the grid at that node, and src/modules/roads/showcase.js:27-30 confirms it: AVE_Z = 40 and the avenue chain runs through x=40 while the north-south street chain also passes (40,40). The avenue is 24 m wide with asphaltHalf 8.0 and cornerR 8 (network.js:9), so the geometrically correct envelope there is materially larger than 34 x 34 m. A builder either restages the scene to match the item (contradicting §8 and the intersection camera's own description) or fails a numeric acceptance item for building exactly what §8 asked for. This is the single most expensive defect in the document: it is a hard number, on the hero preset, that cannot be met as staged.
gaps.fix: Rewrite the sentence as: 'For the avenue x street crossing at (40, 40) (avenue asphaltHalf 8, cornerR 8; street asphaltHalf 5, cornerR 6) the paved square measures <= 40 x 40 m', and recompute the number from max(arm.trim) + 2.0 m using the shipped TYPE_DEFAULTS rather than asserting a street/street case. If a street/street case is genuinely wanted, name a node from showcase.js where two streets actually cross (e.g. (120, 100)) and keep 34 x 34 m for that one.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) / 3 (numeric) — self-contradiction with the spec's own conventions block
gaps.problem: Item 13 is assigned to the 480-px whole-frame scale by the conventions block, then asks the critic to distinguish 'avenue by 4 lanes + double-solid centre', 'street by 2 lanes + dashed centre' and 'alley by ... no centre line' at that scale. The same conventions block states, three paragraphs earlier, that 'at 480 px a 0.10-0.15 m edge line is sub-pixel and its measured value is asphalt, not paint'. At aerial (520 m, pitch 0.85) a 480-px-wide frame is roughly 1 px per metre, so a 0.15 m dashed centre line is ~0.15 px and a double-solid pair with a 0.10-0.15 m gap is ~0.4 px. The item therefore asks for a discrimination the spec has already declared unmeasurable at the scale it assigns. The builder cannot know whether to widen paint (violating item 6's 0.10-0.15 m widths) or ignore the item; the critic can fail or pass it at will.
gaps.fix: Split item 13. Keep at 480 px only what is width- and band-based and survives at ~1 px/m: carriageway width ordering (highway > avenue > street > alley), the median gap on the highway, the sidewalk band delta (dL >= 18) and the asphalt-vs-ground delta (dL >= 25). Move every paint-based discriminator (dashed vs double-solid vs no centre line, gravel's absence of paint) to a named full-resolution crop of aerial_12 — e.g. aerial_12_HIERARCHY_<type>.png at >= 256 px per type — and say so, so the two scales stop contradicting each other.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — a required measurement whose subject may not exist in the named shots
gaps.problem: Item 4 requires a complete four-crop set including a SHADOW CROP from BOTH street_12 and armtop_12, and grades mean L(CARRIAGEWAY)/mean L(SHADOW) >= 2.0. The SHADOW CROP is defined as >= 128 x 64 px of asphalt in cast shadow from a kerb, parapet, barrier or deck soffit, taken from the same shot. armtop_12 is a top-down view over one avenue arm at ~40 m: it contains no parapet, no barrier and no deck soffit, and at noon a 0.15 m kerb casts a shadow a few centimetres wide — nowhere near a 128 x 64 px region of shadowed asphalt. street_12 (60 m, pitch 0.18) has the same problem. Every other item in the document that could be unsatisfiable carries an explicit fallback (the 60 m crop may be split in two; heapMB null is 'ungraded, not failed'), so the omission here reads as an oversight rather than a deliberate stretch — and it lands on the item the spec itself ranks fourth by score impact.
gaps.fix: Restrict the lit/shadow ratio to shots that actually contain a shadow caster of the right size — bridge_12 (deck soffit / parapet) and hillcut_12 (retaining wall) — and name those two SHADOW CROPs explicitly. For street_12 and armtop_12, either drop the SHADOW CROP from the required set or replace the ratio with a kerb-shadow measurement matched to the real feature size (e.g. a >= 64 x 8 px gutter-shadow run), and add the standard fallback sentence: 'if no qualifying shadow region >= the stated size exists in that shot, report it as absent and the sub-item is ungraded.'

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — an automatic-fail criterion with no observation path
gaps.problem: Item 22 says 'The probe records the index bounds it wrote; any vertex outside the corridor + graded slope is an automatic fail.' A critic's throwaway Playwright probe cannot record what the module wrote to world.terrain.heights during init — it attaches after window.__sim.ready, and nothing in the frozen api (§2: stats() -> {edges,nodes,meshes,tris,bridges,terrainVerts,ms}) exposes the written index range. Worse, §2's 'Permitted additions this round' reads as a closed list (opts.width and debug.setVisible only), so a conscientious builder may believe it is forbidden from adding the very accessor the item needs. Contrast item 19, which is checkable precisely because terrainVerts already exists. As written, the strictest fail condition in the spec is unverifiable.
gaps.fix: Add to the permitted-additions list: 'api.debug.terrainWrites() -> [{ix0, iz0, ix1, iz1, edgeId}] — the heightfield index rectangles this module wrote on the last rebuild', and rewrite item 22 to read: 'the probe calls api.debug.terrainWrites(), converts each rectangle to world coordinates, and checks every vertex in it lies inside the corridor half-width + GRADE_REACH of some edge; any vertex outside is an automatic fail.'

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — implementation requirements with no named observation method
gaps.problem: Item 7 ends with a stranded sentence: 'Roughness >= 0.55 beyond 60 m, normalScale faded to <= 0.25 beyond 120 m, anisotropy = ctx.assets.anisotropy on every road map, dash coverage box-filtered.' These are four separate requirements about shader/material state, appended to an item whose grading is a pixel statistic. None of them is observable in a screenshot, a JSON log or a page-evaluate probe as the spec's §4 preamble requires ('each item observable in a screenshot, a JSON log, or a page-evaluate probe'). The critic must either read the shader source (which CRITIC.md permits but this item does not say) or ignore them; the builder cannot tell which sub-clauses are graded.
gaps.fix: Either (a) move these four to a probe: 'api.debug.materialParams() -> {roughnessFar, normalScaleFar, anisotropy, dashFilter}' with the four thresholds checked from the returned object, or (b) demote them to a 'how to pass this item' note explicitly marked as guidance, not an acceptance clause — with one sentence saying the graded quantity for item 7 is only the <= 0.05 % speckle number on the three named regions.

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — thresholds carried into a regime where they are below noise or unachievable
gaps.problem: Item 15 applies one threshold set to both the 17.5 and the 22 rain sessions. At 22:00 item 14 puts the CARRIAGEWAY p50 at 8-38, so 'WET p50 is >= 12 % below DRY's' is a 1-4 level difference — inside SwiftShader/AgX quantisation noise, and the spec offers no tolerance. The specular clause is worse: '>= 0.5 % of the carriageway region above DRY's p99 + 25' at 22:00, in a showcase where the standing assumptions state there are no lamps of any kind and roads may add none, leaves only the moon as a specular source; a grazing moon glint covering half a percent of the carriageway is a strong claim to make without evidence it is achievable. Separately, the reversibility clause ('>= 99.9 % of DRY2's pixels within +/-1 level of DRY's') never says over which region — whole frame or the crops — and a whole-frame reading pulls in terrain grass and any residual animation.
gaps.fix: State the thresholds per hour: keep the >= 12 % p50 drop, the specular clause and the paint ratio for 17.5; for 22 replace the percentage drop with an absolute one ('WET p50 is >= 4 levels below DRY's') and either drop the specular clause or lower it to '>= 0.1 % of the carriageway region above DRY's p99 + 15, or report that the moon geometry in this shot produces no grazing highlight'. Add 'over the union of the CARRIAGEWAY and PAINT crop rectangles' to the reversibility clause.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — a statistic the spec's own rule renders ungraded
gaps.problem: Item 5(c) requires 'a gutter grime band 0.4-0.8 m wide along every kerb, 6-18 L darker' — a per-material luminance statistic. The conventions block routes every statistic in items 3-8 to a named full-resolution crop and declares that 'a statistic whose crop is not saved and named is ungraded'. But the four named crop types are CARRIAGEWAY, SIDEWALK, PAINT and SHADOW, and CARRIAGEWAY is explicitly defined to contain 'no kerb'. There is therefore no crop in which 5(c) can legally be measured, so by the spec's own rule the item nullifies itself. (Item 3(b) hits the same wall and solves it by inventing a kerb-face crop inline; 5(c) does not.) A related tension: the armtop_12 CARRIAGEWAY crop must span >= 60 m of carriageway (item 5a) while containing no manhole and no seam, on a surface item 5(b)/(d) require to carry >= 1 cover per 40 m of lane and >= 2 seams per 100 m — satisfiable only with a carefully chosen narrow strip, which the spec should say out loud.
gaps.fix: Add a fifth named crop to the conventions block: 'GUTTER CROP — a >= 128 x 32 px run along the kerb line including the gutter band and 0.5 m of adjacent carriageway, saved as <shot>_GUTTER.png', and have 5(c) read 'mean L(gutter band) is 6-18 levels below mean L(the adjacent carriageway strip in the same GUTTER CROP)'. Add one sentence to the crop rules: 'the CARRIAGEWAY crop may be a long narrow strip along one lane; spanning 60 m while avoiding covers and seams is expected to require that shape.'

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — the spec's own consistency argument applied to draw calls but not to triangles
gaps.problem: §5 argues persuasively that the declared budget in index.js must be 48 so that 'CRITIC.md's draw calls within the declared budget and the row below are the same test'. That argument is not applied to triangles: index.js currently declares triangles: 600_000 (src/modules/roads/index.js:23) and §5 leaves it there, while the spec's own row caps roads-attributable triangles at 300 000. A build at 450 k triangles passes CRITIC.md's budget gate and fails item 20 — exactly the split-verdict the draw-call paragraph exists to prevent.
gaps.fix: Change the first budget row to '{ drawCalls: 48, triangles: 300_000 }' and extend the existing rationale sentence to cover triangles: 'a 450 k build must not pass the role file and fail the spec'. If 600 k is deliberately kept as headroom for later waves, say so and mark item 20's triangle row as the binding one.

gaps.problem: ROADS REGION is defined as 'the pixels covered by asphalt + sidewalk + bridge structure', but the isolation procedure (capture, setVisible(false), 5 frames, |dL| > 6) also captures every terrain pixel that was in a road-cast shadow, plus any pixel where a road mesh was occluding brighter background. Item 14 then takes 'zero pixels > 225' and 'mean(B) - mean(R) >= +5' over that superset. At 22:00 the moon is weak so contamination is probably small, but at the very least the definition and the procedure should not disagree in a document this precise, and a builder cannot tell whether a bright terrain pixel revealed by hiding a parapet is their finding.
gaps.fix: Add one clause to the ROADS REGION definition: 'pixels that get brighter when roads are hidden are shadow, not road surface; take only pixels where hiding roads changes L by > 6 AND the roads-visible value is the darker of the two, or intersect the diff with the probe's projected road polygon.'

gaps.property: 5 (bounded blast radius) — role-file content restated in the module spec
gaps.problem: Three rules that belong to BUILDER.md/ARCHITECTURE are re-stated here and will drift when the role file changes: §5's geometry rule ('anything repeated more than ~50 times ... is an InstancedMesh or is merged') duplicates BUILDER.md's instancing rule and ARCHITECTURE §2; §7's closing sentence ('Math.random, Date.now() in logic, and writing any world section other than world.roads ... are forbidden') duplicates BUILDER.md's determinism and stay-in-your-lane rules and ARCHITECTURE §11; §2's 'mutate in place; never world.roads = {...}' duplicates BUILDER.md and ARCHITECTURE §3. The spec is elsewhere scrupulous about this (items 19 and 21 and §6's boot-overlay bullet all name the role file instead of copying it), which makes these three stand out as oversights.
gaps.fix: Replace each with a pointer in the style the document already uses: 'instancing threshold and the mutate-never-replace rule are BUILDER.md's; the roads-specific delta is only the per-tile-per-material draw-call accounting below'. Keep only what is roads-specific (tiles <= 1024 m, one draw call per tile x material, and the named repeated objects: manhole covers, guardrail posts, balusters, gullies).

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) / 2 (falsifiable) — two items softer than their neighbours
gaps.problem: Item 17 is the only acceptance item that does not name the shot it is graded in ('name the shot it reads in' delegates that to the builder), and it grades gravel partly on 'a coarser normal', which is not observable as stated. Item 23 asserts '800 ms of api.stats().ms' on 'the 75-edge showcase network' without saying whether 800 ms is a SwiftShader wall-clock number (r1 measured 1.58 s for a full 66-edge rebuild on this box) or a real-GPU one, and without pinning 75 edges to anything in §8 — if the staged scene comes out at 90 edges the item's premise is stale. The standard's property 3 explicitly requires saying when a number cannot be measured in this environment and naming the stand-in.
gaps.fix: For item 17, name the shot per type (gravel in aerial_12 plus a named GRAVEL crop from closeup_12; alley in closeup_12 or a named aerial crop) and replace 'a coarser normal' with a measurable proxy, e.g. 'std of L in a >= 128 x 64 px gravel crop is >= 1.6x the CARRIAGEWAY CROP's'. For item 23, add 'measured under SwiftShader on this box, where a full init rebuild is ~1.5-3.5 s; the item is the ratio as much as the absolute — a dirty-region rebuild must be < 1/3 of a full rebuild measured in the same run', and change '75-edge' to 'the showcase network as staged in §8 (report its edge count)'.

gaps.property: 1 (sequenced) — a directive written as a false statement of fact
gaps.problem: §8 item 9 says 'The r1/r2 coastwest camera is gone from the preset list'. It is not gone: src/modules/roads/showcase.js:10 still defines the coastwest preset. The sentence is a decision presented as an observation, so a builder reading it may believe no action is needed and leave a tenth preset registered, breaking the 'exactly these nine, no more' rule and the 38-capture manifest.
gaps.fix: Rewrite as an instruction: 'Remove the coastwest preset from CAMERAS and from the registered set (showcase.js:10) — showcase.cameras must be exactly the nine in the table. The coast transition does not stop being graded: item 8 probes it as a terminus and the report carries aerial_12_COASTEND.png.'

strengths: World-data block in §2 is a genuine verbatim copy of ARCHITECTURE §3's roads section (diffed line by line: identical modulo indentation, only the 'terrain owes:' comment dropped, and that omission is covered explicitly in the standing assumptions). The 'frozen shapes' addendum correctly records the isRoad -> 0|1|2 superset that terrain already consumes, and names breaking it an automatic fail.

Every dependency API I spot-checked exists at the cited location: world.terrain.getHeight/getNormal/getSlope/isWater/raycast/modify/heights/features are live; ctx.modules.terrain.data()/stats()/setReflection()/setGrassTufts()/material()/debug{} match src/modules/terrain/index.js:150-162 including debug.waterRT() at :162; environment's setupMaterial/hookScene/getSunDirection/getMoonDirection/getLightDirection/getExposure/getNight are at index.js:313-321; assets.pbr/applyPbr/procedural.noiseTexture/gradient/anisotropy, camera.registerPreset, rng.float/int/range/pick/weighted/gauss/shuffle/fork, events.on(name,fn,owner), and LAYERS.ROADS/RENDER_ORDER.ROADS=20/MARKINGS=21 all match src/core/. The spec is right that writeHeights/flattenStrip do NOT exist yet (grep returns nothing in src/modules/terrain/) and correctly mandates feature-detection plus the round-2 fallback.

The probe access-path block is the strongest part of the document: window.__sim.world.roads, registry.apis.roads, registry.get('roads').group, stats() field list, and the explicit 'There is no window.__sim.modules' all match src/core/debug.js:13-32 and registry.js exactly. This single paragraph removes the most common source of wasted critic rounds.

Numeric density is exceptional and the quoted code constants are accurate: kerb 0.13-0.18 m vs KERB_H=0.15, cornerR alley 4 / gravel 4 / street 6 / avenue 8 / highway 10 / ramp 8 vs TYPE_DEFAULTS network.js:6-12, street asphaltHalf 5.0, coverage res 512 / cell 4 vs build.js:519, the 15% grade in r2 vs MAX_GRADE=0.15 in build.js:21. The 'the code value wins and the quote is there to save a lookup' rule pre-empts a whole class of argument.

Known failure modes (§6) are all real and traceable to this project: terrain teeth (r1 blocker 1), grass through asphalt (r1 blocker 2), bald discs, floating deck ends / black cliff (r1 blocker 3), washed-out noon p1>=97 (r1 issue 4), the packed-integer non-flat varying speckle (r1 issue 5, root-caused in r2's build record), square roundabout (r1 issue 7), fillet over crosswalk (r1 issue 8), pier caps (issue 9), tiling (issue 10), hooked L arrows (issue 11), non-idempotent rebuild 45922->45524 (issue 13). Zero generic advice.

Role-file discipline is deliberate and mostly clean: item 21 and item 19 explicitly say what BUILDER.md/CRITIC.md already cover and add only the delta; §6's boot-overlay bullet explicitly refuses to restate SwiftShader mechanics; item 22 states the corridor exception as a named delta to 'stay in your lane' rather than re-copying it.

The capture manifest is a genuinely closed set and it balances: 16+9+5+6+1+1 = 38, and every shot named in items 1-24 (street_6p5, armtop_12, overpass_22, roundabout_22, rain_wet_17p5, aerial_12_720p, all_aerial_12 ...) resolves inside it. Crops are excluded from the count explicitly.

The measurement-conventions block solves the r1/r2 argument about scale: two named scales, a rule that per-material statistics are never taken at 480 px, one crop per material per shot with a fixed filename, world-extent reporting so 'per N metres' is computable, and the 'unsaved crop = ungraded, not failed' rule that stops a critic inventing evidence.

Item 7's explicit exemption of marking edges from the sparkle test (with the reasoning that blurring markings to pass is itself a finding), item 8's speckle-as-a-delta-not-a-level rule with terrain named as the owner of the water RT, and item 15's rejection of `--weather rain` in favour of a scripted three-capture session with the actual wetness ramp quoted from environment/index.js:198 are all places where the spec anticipates a specific bad outcome and closes it.
verdict: 8.0 — a strong spec that misses the 8.5 bar on internal consistency, not on ambition. It is in the top decile of what I have reviewed for properties 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10: the world-data block is a verified verbatim copy of ARCHITECTURE §3, every dependency API I checked exists at the cited file and line (terrain debug.waterRT() at index.js:162, environment's api at index.js:313-321, the __sim surface at debug.js:13-32, and the correct observation that terrain.writeHeights/flattenStrip do not exist yet), the quoted code constants match TYPE_DEFAULTS and build.js exactly, the failure-mode list is entirely traceable to roads_r1.md and the r2 build record with no generic filler, the 38-shot manifest is closed and balances, and role-file duplication is mostly avoided on purpose. Budget is consistent with ARCHITECTURE §9 (48 of the allotted 80 draw calls, sub-2 ms per frame, sub-15 s init) and the draw-call rationale is exactly right. Where it fails is Lens 2. Of 24 acceptance items, five would produce an argument on first contact: item 12 grades a numeric envelope at a node the staged scene builds differently (avenue x street, not street x street — showcase.js:27-30); item 13 asks the critic to resolve dashed and double-solid centre lines at the one scale the spec's own conventions block declares sub-pixel; item 4 demands a 128 x 64 px asphalt-in-shadow crop from two noon shots that contain no shadow caster of that size, with none of the fallback language the document uses everywhere else; item 22's automatic-fail condition has no probe-visible accessor and §2's closed additions list arguably forbids adding one; item 7's tail sets four shader-state requirements with no observation method. Add item 5(c) nullifying itself under the spec's own unsaved-crop rule and item 15 carrying daytime thresholds into a moonlit frame where a 12 % drop is one or two levels, and roughly a fifth of the checklist is either unbuildable-as-written or ungradeable. None of this is structural — every one of the twelve gaps is a surgical edit to a named sentence, and fixing the top five would put this at 9.0. But as it stands two competent builders would not produce the same intersection envelope or the same aerial paint widths, and the critic and builder would spend a round arguing about a shadow crop that does not exist. That is a 8.0, not a 8.5.
